propositions: The reconciler re-attempts structurally-impossible inbound link writes every pass because failed links never generate LINK events, so identical impossible records are re-emitted without memory of prior failure

Four consecutive live passes each emit exactly 19 identical failing inbound link writes (5 closed-source, 13 redundant-ancestry, 1 would-create-cycle), forming a permanent WARNING log floor that obscures genuine faults
The applier catches link failures with warn-and-continue, lacking durable storage to distinguish permanent structural impossibilities from transient I/O faults
A durable store keyed on classify()→reason and a digest over the structural inputs the three validators read will skip re-attempts when the digest matches and only re-attempt when those inputs change
The impossible_links.json file must be staged and committed to the tickets branch by _commit_binding_store_snapshot, so records survive process restarts and CI checkouts between passes

Cycle records must key on the global structural projection because check_would_create_cycle walks the transitive graph, so an intermediate ticket change can break a cycle despite endpoint digests remaining unchanged
